newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fruit of the Loom no comment on CEO report.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom no comment on CEO report.

text.p: A spokesman for U.S. textile manufacturer Fruit of the Loom declined comment on Friday on reports that Andy McCarter, director of spinning operations, would replace his brother as head of the Irish unit.
"We've absolutely no comment to make," a spokesman for the company, one of Ireland's biggest manufacturers, said of a report on the Irish Times and on state RTE radio.

The reports said that Andy McCarter would be offered the position of Chief Executive of the Irish unit in succession to his brother, who is seeking an injunction against a redundancy notice in the Dublin courts.

The Londonderry-born businessman, his brother John and finance director Seamus McEleney were served with redundancy notices by the U.S. Fruit of the Loom Corporation which owns 100 percent of the Irish businesses.
The matter is currently before the courts and affidavits from all three have yet to be officially opened, sources close to the company said.
The case is not expected to be heard for up to two weeks, court officials said.
Ireland's Enterprise and Employment Minister, Mary Harney, is expected to travel to Chicago to discuss the matter with Fruit of the Loom's parent company, official sources said.
Tourism and Sport Minister Jim McDaid told RTE he was extremely worried that the dispute would put jobs at risk at the company's Donegal plants.
McDaid's statement echoed concerns voiced by Ireland's main trade union, SIPTU, about possible job losses in an unemployment black spot in Donegal.
He said he expected Harney, who is currently on holiday in Italy, to meet Fruit of the Loom's chief executive in Chicago at the end of the month.
On Thursday the company issued a statement confirming that redundancy notices had been issued to three executives and said their positions were not being filled.
It said the company was committed to its Irish operation and said business would continue as normal.

It was the company's first formal statement on media reports suggesting that the dispute dated back to the start of the year, when some of McCarter's responsibilities were transferred back to the United States.
Andy McCarter is director of spinning operations in Londonderry, Northern Ireland, part of a cross-border business which includes five plants in Donegal, in the Irish republic.
The company employs around 3,500 people in Ireland and in Northern Ireland in what is seen by the British and Irish governments as a model cross-border operation.
In 1986, U.S. Fruit of the Loom bought McCarter's Ireland interests in Derry and Donegal from the McCarter family, and Willie McCarter was appointed managing director of the Irish operations in 1987.

Media reports suggest files at the Company Records office show that Fruit of the Loom in Ireland slid into the red, recording a pre-tax loss of 13.5 million Irish pounds ($19.6 million) in 1995 down from a profit of 5.8 million in 1994.

McCarter is heavily involved in cross border relations and is chairman of the International Fund for Ireland, a multinational private fund which collects and distributes investment in Irish projects ($ = 0.689 Irish Pounds)
